title: Workspaces and Monorepos
description: Link local packages, hoist dependencies, and run tasks across a monorepo with npm, Yarn, and pnpm workspaces.

data.text: A **monorepo** keeps several packages in one repository. **Workspaces** make the package manager aware of them: local packages are symlinked into `node_modules` instead of being published, and shared dependencies are hoisted to the root.

data.title: Benefits
items: Atomic commits across packages — a breaking change and its call sites land together.
Shared tooling: one TypeScript, ESLint, and test config.
Local packages resolve without publishing to a registry.
Easier to enforce consistent versions and run affected-only CI.

data.caption: Root package.json with workspaces (npm, Yarn, pnpm-compatible)

data.text: The root `package.json` is `"private": true` because workspaces are never published as a single package. pnpm uses the same globs in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` instead.

data.title: Add a dependency to one package, not the root
data.code:
# npm
npm install zod --workspace packages/ui
npm run test --workspace packages/ui

# Yarn
cd packages/ui && yarn add zod
yarn workspace ui run test

# pnpm
pnpm add zod --filter @acme/ui
pnpm --filter @acme/ui test

data.text: Inside the repo, packages reference each other with a workspace range. npm and pnpm understand `workspace:*`; Yarn Berry requires the protocol. This guarantees the local version is linked while developing.

Hoisting lifts compatible versions of a package to the root `node_modules` so they are installed once. It saves disk space and install time, but it also means a package can import a dependency it never declared (phantom dependency) — code that works locally can fail when published. pnpm and Yarn PnP refuse phantom dependencies, which is exactly why they catch these bugs early.

data.caption: How workspaces link and hoist packages
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Root package.json workspaces globs] --> B[Resolve each package]
    B --> C[Symlink @acme/ui into node_modules]
    B --> D[Hoist shared deps once at root]
    C --> E[apps/app imports @acme/ui]
    D --> E

data.title: One lockfile, one install
data.text: In a workspace monorepo the lockfile lives at the root. Run installs from the root, not from each package, or you will create divergent trees.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Workspaces symlink local packages and hoist shared dependencies.
The root manifest is private; the root lockfile governs every package.
Reference siblings with workspace:* so the local version is always linked.
Hoisting is fast but hides phantom dependencies — strict managers surface them.
data.takeaway: Monorepos trade repository size for atomic changes; workspaces are the tool that makes that trade practical.
